newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian SIDANKO oil fails to regain Purneftegaz.
newsitem.headline: Russian SIDANKO oil fails to regain Purneftegaz.

text.p: Russia's SIDANKO oil company lost its bid to regain ownership of key crude producer Purneftegaz as the arbitration court ruled on Monday that competitor Rosneft could keep the enterprise.
Vladimir Vetluzhky, a member of the court, told Reuters that the body had ruled against SIDANKO's bid to require the government to force Rosneft to give it Purneftegaz.
A 1994 government resolution awarded Purneftegaz to SIDANKO (the Siberian-Far Eastern Oil Company), but a 1995 ruling shifted ownership of the producer to Rosneft.
The changes were part of the government's reshaping of the once state-run oil sector into vertically-integrated companies.
The decision is widely seen as a victory for Rosneft, the state oil holding company which is being privatised but which has lost many of its assets under restructuring.
It was not immediately clear whether there would be an appeal.
Purneftegaz shares traded at $2.30 on the Russian Trading System at 1110 GMT, up 2.22 percent on Friday's close.
